== Three people carry a "composer" ({{P|106}}) occupation with no documented musical work behind it ==

This is a genuine request for Wikidata editors to double-check, not a confirmed
error on either side — we (a third-party database of concert-music composers,
not affiliated with Wikidata) found these three while auditing our own data and
couldn't independently verify the composer tag against any source, but we may
simply have missed one.

'''Leó Popper''' ([[Q1239198]]) carries four {{P|106}} values: art historian
([[Q1792450]]), painter ([[Q1028181]]), composer ([[Q36834]]), and art critic
([[Q4164507]]). Wikidata's own short description is "painter (1886-1911)" —
no mention of composing. His Hungarian Wikipedia article (linked above)
describes him only as "magyar művészettörténész, festő, kritikus" (Hungarian
art historian, painter, critic) and gives no biographical detail suggesting
any musical activity. He is the son of the cellist-composer David Popper ([[Q354927]]), which may
be how the composer tag was originally added (by association with his
father rather than his own work), but we found no direct source for it.

'''Celina Szymanowska''' ([[Q5058073]]) has exactly one {{P|106}} value:
composer ([[Q36834]]), and no other occupation claim at all. Wikidata's own
short description is "wife of Polish poet Adam Mickiewicz (1812–1855)". Both
her English and Polish Wikipedia articles (linked above — Polish being her
native language and the more detailed of the two) describe her exclusively
as the daughter of composer/pianist Maria Szymanowska and the wife of poet
Adam Mickiewicz, mother of his six children — neither mentions any
composition, performance, or other musical activity of her own, despite
fairly detailed biographical coverage in both.

'''Royden Barrie''' ([[Q19600352]], a pseudonym used by Rodney Bennett) carries
four {{P|106}} values including composer ([[Q36834]]), alongside poet
([[Q36180]]) and writer ([[Q49757]]). Wikidata's own short description is
"British writer and poet" — no mention of composing. His English Wikipedia
article (linked above) describes him as a playwright, children's author, and
lyricist who wrote words for songs by Eric Coates, Hayden Wood, Roger Quilter,
and Martin Shaw — i.e. he supplied the words, not the music, for those songs.
He is the father of the actual composer Richard Rodney Bennett, which may be
the same kind of by-association mix-up as the Popper case above.

'''Why we're reporting this instead of just fixing our own data:''' unlike
the William Reed case in this same directory, this isn't a QID-matching bug
on our side — we're confident these are the correct Wikidata items for all
three people, we're just unable to confirm the composer occupation claim
itself from either their Wikidata entry's references or the Wikipedia
articles linked from it. If a source does exist for any of them actually
having composed something, please disregard this note — we'd genuinely
rather be wrong here than remove a real (if minor/uncredited) composer's
data.

(For context: all three were removed from our own composers database as a
result of this finding, since our project's scope is specifically people
whose primary documented reputation is as a composer of concert music.)
